Also known as: Total Recordable Incident Rate
Definition: How often work-related injuries serious enough to need medical treatment are happening, adjusted so plants or teams of different sizes can be compared fairly.

Also known as: Lost Time Incident Rate; LTIFR
Definition: How often injuries happen that are serious enough to cause someone to miss work, adjusted for team size so different periods or sites can be compared fairly.

Also known as: DART Rate
Definition: How often injuries happen that are serious enough to cause days away from work, restricted duty, or a job transfer.

Also known as: Near Misses
Definition: Incidents that could have caused harm but didn't. Tracking these closely helps catch safety issues before someone actually gets hurt.

Also known as: Gemba Walk
Definition: “Gemba” means “the real place” -- the shop floor. A Gemba walk is a scheduled walkthrough where leaders check conditions in person rather than from a desk.

Also known as: 5S Audit
Definition: A workplace-organization standard covering five habits: Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, and Sustain. A 5S score reflects how well an area is following it.
Personal Protective Equipment -- the gear (gloves, goggles, hard hats, etc.) workers wear to stay safe on the job.

Also known as: Corrective and Preventive Action; Corrective Action
Definition: The formal process of fixing the immediate cause of a safety or quality issue (corrective) and changing the process so it doesn't happen again (preventive).

Also known as: Action Item Closure
Definition: The share of open follow-up items -- issues flagged in an audit, walk, or review -- that have actually been resolved.

Also known as: Safety Rating
Definition: An overall measure of how well safety requirements are being met.

Also known as: Incidents; Accidents
Definition: Events at work that caused, or could have caused, injury or damage.

Also known as: First Aid
Definition: Minor work injuries treated on site without needing professional medical treatment.

Also known as: LTI
Definition: Work injuries that caused the employee to miss one or more days of work.

Also known as: Recordable Incidents; Recordable Cases; Recordables
Definition: The number of work injuries and illnesses serious enough to be recorded under safety rules, because they need more than first aid.

Also known as: Lost Time Frequency Rate
Definition: The number of injuries causing lost working time for every million hours worked.

Also known as: TRIFR; Recordable Injury Frequency Rate
Definition: The number of recordable injuries for every million hours worked.

Also known as: Injury Severity Rate; Incident Severity Rate
Definition: The number of working days lost because of injuries for every million hours worked. It shows how serious injuries are, not only how many there are.

Also known as: Days Away; Restricted Days; DART Days
Definition: The number of days people were away from work, or on restricted or changed duties, because of a work injury or illness.

Also known as: Lost Days; Days Lost; Lost Time Days
Definition: The total number of working days lost because of work injuries and illnesses.

Also known as: Fatality Rate; Work-Related Deaths; Fatal Accidents
Definition: The number of deaths caused by work. The aim is always zero.

Also known as: Exposure Hours; Man-Hours; Total Hours Worked
Definition: The total hours worked by all employees and contractors in a period. It is the base used to work out safety rates.

Also known as: Days Since Last Accident; Days Since Last LTI; Safe Days
Definition: The number of days that have passed since the last injury that caused lost working time.

Also known as: Incident Frequency Rate; Accident Frequency Rate; Accident Rate
Definition: The number of incidents for each fixed number of hours worked, so that different sites can be compared fairly.

Also known as: Number of Incidents; Total Incidents; Incidents Reported
Definition: The total number of safety incidents recorded in a period.

Also known as: Near Misses Reported; Near Miss Frequency; Near-Miss Rate
Definition: The number of near misses reported for each fixed number of hours worked or employees. A higher figure is good because it shows people are speaking up.

Also known as: Hazards Reported; Hazards Identified; Unsafe Conditions Reported
Definition: The number of unsafe conditions or acts that people reported before anyone was hurt.

Also known as: Hazards Closed; Hazards Resolved
Definition: The share of reported hazards that have been fixed and closed.

Also known as: Overdue Actions; Open Safety Actions; Outstanding Actions
Definition: The number of safety actions that are still waiting to be finished, often with a count of those past their due date.

Also known as: Time to Close Action; Average Closure Time
Definition: The average number of days taken to close a safety action from when it was raised.

Also known as: Investigations Completed; Investigation Closure Rate
Definition: The share of incidents that were investigated and closed within the target time.

Also known as: Inspections Done; Safety Walks; Workplace Inspections
Definition: The number or share of planned safety inspections that were carried out.

Also known as: Behaviour Observations; Behavior-Based Safety Observations; BBS Observations
Definition: The number of checks where a person watches how work is done and notes safe and unsafe behaviour.

Also known as: Safe Behavior Percentage; Percent Safe; Safe Acts
Definition: The share of observed behaviours that were safe.

Also known as: Safety Audit Rating; EHS Audit Score; Safety Compliance Score
Definition: The overall score given after a safety audit, showing how well the site meets the requirements.

Also known as: EHS Audit Findings; Audit Non-Compliances
Definition: The number of gaps or breaches found during safety audits.

Also known as: Safety Training Rate; EHS Training Compliance; Induction Completion
Definition: The share of required safety training that has been completed by the people who need it.

Also known as: Hours of Safety Training; EHS Training Hours
Definition: The total hours spent on safety training in a period.

Also known as: Safety Briefings; Tool Box Talks; Safety Meetings Held
Definition: The number of short safety talks given to work teams, usually before a shift or a job.

Also known as: Safety Briefing Attendance; Attendance at Safety Meetings
Definition: The share of people who attended the planned safety meetings or briefings.

Also known as: Fire Drills; Evacuation Drills; Drills Conducted
Definition: The number or share of planned emergency drills that were carried out.

Also known as: PTW Compliance; Work Permit Compliance; Permits Issued
Definition: The share of high-risk jobs carried out with the correct work permit in place.

Also known as: LOTO Compliance; Isolation Compliance
Definition: The share of checks where machines were correctly locked off and tagged before work started.

Also known as: PPE Usage; PPE Compliance Rate; Protective Equipment Compliance
Definition: The share of checks in which people were wearing the protective equipment their task needs.

Also known as: Risk Assessment Completion; Risk Assessments Reviewed; JSA Completion
Definition: The share of jobs or areas that have an up-to-date risk assessment.

Also known as: High Risk Hazards; Critical Findings; High Severity Findings
Definition: The number of hazards or audit findings rated as high risk, which need quick action.

Also known as: Critical Equipment Checks; Safety Equipment Inspection Compliance
Definition: The share of safety-critical equipment, such as fire extinguishers, alarms and guards, that was inspected on time.

Also known as: MTC; Medical Treatment Injuries
Definition: The number of injuries that needed medical treatment beyond first aid.

Also known as: RWC; Restricted Work Injuries; Modified Duty Cases
Definition: The number of injuries after which a person could work only in a limited way.

Also known as: First Aid Injury Rate; FAC Rate
Definition: The number of first aid cases for every million hours worked.

Also known as: Property Damage; Damage Incidents; Equipment Damage Incidents
Definition: The number of incidents that damaged equipment, buildings or other property.

Also known as: Motor Vehicle Accidents; Vehicle Accidents; Driving Incidents
Definition: The number of accidents involving company vehicles or drivers, often shown per million kilometres driven.

Also known as: Spills; Environmental Releases; Environmental Non-Compliances
Definition: The number of events that harmed or could have harmed the environment, such as chemical spills or illegal discharges.

Also known as: Regulatory Compliance Rate; Legal Compliance; EHS Compliance
Definition: The share of environmental and safety legal requirements that the site is meeting.

Also known as: Notices of Violation; Enforcement Notices; Fines and Penalties
Definition: The number of formal notices, fines or penalties received from safety or environmental regulators.

Also known as: Workers' Comp Cost; Injury Cost; Cost of Injuries
Definition: The money paid out or set aside for compensation and treatment because of work injuries.

Also known as: EMR; Experience Mod; Insurance Mod
Definition: A figure used by insurers to adjust the price of workers' compensation cover based on the business's own claims record compared with similar businesses. Below 1 is better than average.

Also known as: Safety Climate Score; Safety Perception Score; Safety Survey Score
Definition: A score from a staff survey about how safe people feel and how seriously safety is taken in their workplace.

Also known as: Safety Ideas; Safety Improvement Ideas
Definition: The number of ideas people put forward to make work safer.

Also known as: Ergonomic Risk Assessments; Ergonomic Reviews Completed
Definition: The number of workstations or tasks checked for strain and posture risks.

Also known as: Occupational Disease Rate; Work-Related Illness Rate
Definition: The number of illnesses caused by work, such as hearing loss or skin conditions, for each fixed number of hours worked.

Also known as: Medical Surveillance Completion; Health Checks Completed
Definition: The share of employees who had their planned health checks, such as hearing or lung tests.

Also known as: Hazardous Substance Register; Safety Data Sheet Compliance; SDS Compliance
Definition: The share of hazardous chemicals on site that are listed in the register and have a current safety data sheet.

Also known as: Contractor TRIR; Contractor Safety Rating; Contractor Incident Rate
Definition: The safety results of outside contractors working on site, such as their incident rate or audit score.

Also known as: Contractor Safety Pre-Qual; Contractor Approval Rate
Definition: The share of contractors who passed the safety checks before being allowed to work on site.

Also known as: Leadership Safety Tours; Manager Safety Visits; Visible Felt Leadership
Definition: The number of times managers went out to the work area to talk about safety and check conditions.

Also known as: Stop Work Events; Work Stoppages for Safety
Definition: The number of times someone stopped a job because they believed it was unsafe. A higher figure can mean people feel free to speak up.

Also known as: Observation Closure; Observations Closed
Definition: The share of safety observations that have been dealt with and closed.

Also known as: Site Incident Rate; Incident Rate by Location
Definition: The incident rate shown for each site or department so that they can be compared.
